how-java-works.title: Hello World with JVM Info
how-java-works.description: Write a Java program that prints 'Hello, Java!' and also prints the Java version using `System.getProperty("java.version")`.
hints: Use System.out.println() for printing.
System.getProperty("java.version") returns the current JRE version string.

how-java-works.title: Class vs Object Demo
how-java-works.description: Create a `Car` class with fields `brand` and `year`. Instantiate two different Car objects and print both their details. This demonstrates how one class blueprint creates multiple objects.
hints: Use `this.brand = brand` inside the constructor.
Create objects with `new Car("Toyota", 2020)`.

variables-primitive-types.title: Type Casting and Overflow
variables-primitive-types.description: Declare an `int` with value 2147483647 (Integer.MAX_VALUE). Add 1 to it and print the result — observe integer overflow. Then use a `long` to hold the correct value and print it.
hints: int + 1 wraps around to Integer.MIN_VALUE due to overflow.
Cast to long first: `(long) maxInt + 1` or use `1L`.

variables-primitive-types.title: String vs char Manipulation
variables-primitive-types.description: Given a `String name = "CodePulse"`, print: (1) its length, (2) the first character, (3) the last character, (4) a substring of the first 4 characters.
hints: Use `.length()` not `.length` for String.
Last char: `charAt(name.length() - 1)`.
substring(start, end) — end is exclusive.

oop-fundamentals.title: Create an Animal Hierarchy
oop-fundamentals.description: Define an abstract class `Animal` with fields `name` and `sound`. Create concrete subclasses `Dog` and `Cat` that override `makeSound()`. Instantiate both and call `makeSound()` for each.

testCases.expectedOutput:
Rex says: Woof!
Whiskers says: Meow!

hints: Use the `abstract` keyword for the class and `makeSound()` method.
Each subclass must implement `makeSound()`.
Use `super(name)` in the subclass constructor to call the parent.

oop-fundamentals.title: Encapsulation with BankAccount
oop-fundamentals.description: Create a `BankAccount` class with a private `balance`. Add `deposit(double)`, `withdraw(double)` (no negative balances), and `getBalance()`. Test with deposit 1000, withdraw 250, then attempt to over-withdraw.
hints: Use `private` for the balance field.
In `withdraw`, check if `amount > balance` before subtracting.
Return `balance` in the getter.

oop-fundamentals.title: Polymorphism with Shapes
oop-fundamentals.description: Create an abstract `Shape` class with abstract `area()`. Implement `Circle` (radius) and `Rectangle` (width, height). Use a `Shape[]` to print areas formatted to 2 decimal places.
hints: Circle area = Math.PI * r * r.
Use `%.2f%n` in printf for 2 decimal places.
Store shapes as Shape[] and iterate polymorphically.

constructors.title: Constructor Overloading
constructors.description: Create a `Person` class with three constructors: no-arg (name='Unknown', age=0), name-only, and name+age. Print each variant.
hints: Define three separate constructors with different parameter lists.
You can chain with `this(...)` to avoid duplication.

constructors.title: Builder Pattern Simulation
constructors.description: Create a `Pizza` class using the Builder pattern. It should have fields `size`, `crust`, and `topping`. The builder should allow chaining like: `new Pizza.Builder("Large").crust("Thin").topping("Cheese").build()`.
hints: Each Builder method should set the field and `return this;` for chaining.
The `Pizza` constructor is private — only the Builder can create it.
The inner Builder has access to Pizza's private constructor.

interfaces-fundamentals.title: Implement Comparable for Sorting
interfaces-fundamentals.description: Create a `Student` class that implements `Comparable<Student>` by GPA (descending). Sort 3 students and print in order.
hints: Descending: compare `other.gpa` to `this.gpa` (reversed).
Use `Double.compare(other.gpa, this.gpa)` for floating-point safety.

interfaces-fundamentals.title: Functional Interface with Lambda
interfaces-fundamentals.description: Define a functional interface `MathOperation` with a method `int operate(int a, int b)`. Implement addition, subtraction, and multiplication using lambdas. Call each and print results.
hints: A functional interface has exactly one abstract method.
Lambda syntax: `(a, b) -> a + b`.
Call it like a method: `add.operate(10, 5)`.

exception-handling.title: Custom Exception Hierarchy
exception-handling.description: Create `PaymentException` and `InsufficientFundsException extends PaymentException`. Write `processPayment(amount, balance)` — throws appropriate exception. Catch specifically and print messages.

testCases.expectedOutput:
Funds error: Need 500.0 but only have 200.0
Payment error: Amount must be positive

hints: Catch the more specific exception first.
Pass a descriptive message to `super(message)`.
Throw the most specific exception that fits.

exception-handling.title: Try-With-Resources
exception-handling.description: Create a `Resource` class that implements `AutoCloseable`. In its `use()` method print 'Using resource'. In `close()` print 'Resource closed'. Use it in a try-with-resources block.

testCases.expectedOutput:
Using resource
Resource closed
After try block

hints: Implement `AutoCloseable` and override `close()`.
Syntax: `try (Resource r = new Resource()) { ... }` — close() is called automatically.
`close()` is called even if an exception is thrown.

collection-framework.title: Frequency Counter with HashMap
collection-framework.description: Count frequency of each character in "programming" using a HashMap. Print as 'char: count' sorted alphabetically.
hints: Use TreeMap to auto-sort by key.
`map.merge(key, 1, Integer::sum)` increments count cleanly.
Use `toCharArray()` to iterate characters.

collection-framework.title: ArrayList vs LinkedList
collection-framework.description: Create an `ArrayList<String>` and add 'Java', 'Spring', 'Docker'. Remove the middle element. Then print all remaining. Then do the same with `LinkedList<String>` and print its first and last elements.
hints: Use `remove(Object)` to remove by value (not by index).
LinkedList has `getFirst()` and `getLast()` methods.
`forEach(System.out::println)` prints each element on a new line.

functional-interfaces-lambdas.title: Filter and Transform with Streams
functional-interfaces-lambdas.description: Given a list of integers 1-10, filter odd numbers, square them, sort, and print each.
hints: `filter(n -> n % 2 != 0)` keeps odd numbers.
`map(n -> n * n)` squares each.
Chain `.sorted()` before `.forEach()`.

functional-interfaces-lambdas.title: Group by Length with Collectors
functional-interfaces-lambdas.description: Given a list of words `["apple", "bat", "cat", "door", "ant"]`, group them by their length using `Collectors.groupingBy`. Print each group sorted by key.
hints: Use `Collectors.groupingBy(String::length)` to group.
Pass `TreeMap::new` as the map factory to get sorted keys.
The result is `Map<Integer, List<String>>`.

generics.title: Generic Stack Implementation
generics.description: Implement a generic `Stack<T>` with `push`, `pop` (throws if empty), `peek`, and `isEmpty`. Test with Integer and String.
hints: Use `ArrayList<T>` internally for storage.
Stack is LIFO: pop() removes the last element.
Type parameter T makes it reusable for any type.

generics.title: Bounded Type Parameter (Upper Bound)
generics.description: Write a generic method `sum(List<? extends Number> list)` that returns the sum of all numbers as a double. Test with a list of integers and a list of doubles.
hints: `? extends Number` accepts List<Integer>, List<Double>, etc.
Call `.doubleValue()` on each Number to get a double.
This method works without code duplication for any numeric list.

multithreading-part1.title: Create Threads Two Ways
multithreading-part1.description: Create a thread by (1) extending `Thread` class — print 'Thread1 running'. Create another by (2) implementing `Runnable` — print 'Thread2 running'. Start both.
hints: Extending Thread: override `run()` and call `start()`.
Implementing Runnable: pass it to `new Thread(runnable)` then call `start()`.
Use `.join()` to wait for threads to finish before main exits.

streams.title: Word Count with Streams
streams.description: Given a list of sentences, split each into words, flatten to a single stream, count total words, and also find the longest word.
hints: Use `flatMap(s -> Arrays.stream(s.split(" ")))` to split and flatten.
`.size()` gives total count.
Use `max(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length))` for longest word.

streams.title: Optional Chain
streams.description: Write a method `getCity(String json)` that returns an Optional<String>. If the json contains 'city:', extract and return the city name, otherwise return empty. Use Optional chaining to print or a default.
hints: Split json by space and look for the token 'city:'.
The city name is the next token after 'city:'.
`Optional.of(value)` vs `Optional.empty()` — use `orElse` to unwrap safely.

memory-management.title: Stack vs Heap Demo
memory-management.description: Create a method `createObjects()` that creates local primitives and objects. Demonstrate that changes to a local int don't affect the caller, but changes through an object reference do.
hints: Primitives are passed by value — `x` is not changed.
Objects are passed by reference — `counter.value` changes.
Stack holds local variables; Heap holds objects.

map-hashmap-internals.title: Word Frequency + Top-N
map-hashmap-internals.description: Count word frequency in a sentence and print the top 2 most frequent words sorted by count descending, then alphabetically for ties.
hints: Use `Collectors.groupingBy` with `Collectors.counting()` for frequency.
Sort entries by value descending, then by key ascending.
Use `.limit(2)` to get top 2.

sb-introduction.title: Simulate @SpringBootApplication Scan
sb-introduction.description: Spring Boot scans all classes in the package. Simulate this by creating a `ComponentScanner` that uses reflection to find all classes implementing a `Component` interface and prints their names.
hints: Implement the Component interface in each service class.
Arrays.asList(components) creates the list from varargs.
In real Spring, @ComponentScan does this automatically via classpath scanning.

sb-beans.title: Bean Lifecycle Simulation
sb-beans.description: Simulate Spring's bean lifecycle. Create interface `InitializingBean` with `afterPropertiesSet()`. Create `DatabaseService` that implements it. Print messages at initialization and usage.
hints: Implement `afterPropertiesSet()` — Spring calls it after injection.
In real Spring, use @PostConstruct instead.
The lifecycle order: instantiate → inject → afterPropertiesSet → ready.

sb-beans.title: Singleton vs Prototype Scope
sb-beans.description: Simulate Spring bean scopes. Create a `BeanFactory` that returns the same instance for 'singleton' scope but a new instance for 'prototype' scope. Verify using `==` comparison.
hints: Singleton: use lazy initialization with a static field.
Prototype: always return `new MyBean()`.
`==` compares references, not values.

sb-dependency-injection.title: Constructor Injection Pattern
sb-dependency-injection.description: Implement constructor-based DI. Create `EmailService` and `Logger` interfaces with implementations. Create `UserService` that depends on both via constructor. Test it.

testCases.expectedOutput:
[LOG] Registering: alice@example.com
Email sent to alice@example.com: Welcome!
User registered: alice@example.com

hints: Constructor injection: accept deps as constructor parameters, assign to final fields.
Program to interfaces, not implementations.
In Spring, @Autowired or @RequiredArgsConstructor does this automatically.

sb-annotations.title: Create a Custom Annotation
sb-annotations.description: Create a custom annotation `@Validate` with a `minLength` attribute. Write a method that checks if a String field annotated with @Validate meets the minimum length requirement using reflection.
hints: Use `@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)` to make annotation available at runtime.
Use `obj.getClass().getDeclaredFields()` to get all fields.
`f.setAccessible(true)` to access private fields; `f.getAnnotation(Validate.class)` to read the annotation.

sb-jpa-entity-mapping.title: Model a JPA Entity Manually
sb-jpa-entity-mapping.description: Without using Spring, model a `Product` POJO that represents a JPA entity: fields `id`, `name`, `price`, `category`. Implement `toString()`. Create 3 products, store in a list, filter by category 'Electronics', and print.

testCases.expectedOutput:
Product{id=1, name='Laptop', price=75000.0, category='Electronics'}
Product{id=3, name='Phone', price=40000.0, category='Electronics'}

hints: Model the entity as a plain class — in Spring you'd add @Entity @Id annotations.
Use stream().filter() to select by category.
The toString format must match exactly.

sb-jwt-fundamentals.title: Base64 Encode/Decode JWT Parts
sb-jwt-fundamentals.description: A JWT has 3 parts separated by dots: header.payload.signature (all Base64-encoded). Simulate encoding and decoding the header and payload using Java's `java.util.Base64`.
hints: Use `Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding()` for JWT-safe encoding.
Split by `.` to get the three parts: `token.split("\\.")` .
Decode with `Base64.getUrlDecoder().decode(part)` then `new String(bytes)`.

sb-rest-client.title: Build a Request-Response Model
sb-rest-client.description: Create a `ApiRequest` class with `method`, `url`, `body` fields and an `ApiResponse` class with `statusCode` and `body`. Write a `processRequest(ApiRequest)` method that simulates routing: GET → 200 'OK', POST → 201 'Created', anything else → 405 'Method Not Allowed'.
hints: Use a switch expression (Java 14+) on `req.method`.
GET → 200 OK, POST → 201 Created, others → 405.
In real Spring, @GetMapping/@PostMapping handles this routing automatically.
